title: Market for fish
questionText: A successful health campaign has increased the demand for fish from D1 to D2, as the diagram shows. What has happened to the equilibrium price and quantity of fish?
answers: Both the equilibrium price and quantity rise
The equilibrium price rises but the quantity falls
The equilibrium price falls but the quantity rises
Both the equilibrium price and quantity fall

title: Market for smartphones
questionText: Several new firms have begun manufacturing smartphones, increasing supply from S1 to S2, as shown. What has happened to the equilibrium price and quantity?
answers: Both the equilibrium price and quantity rise
Both the equilibrium price and quantity fall
The equilibrium price falls but the quantity rises
The equilibrium price rises but the quantity falls

title: Market for gym memberships
questionText: A deep recession has sharply reduced household incomes, decreasing the demand for gym memberships from D1 to D2, as shown. What has happened to the equilibrium price and quantity?
answers: The equilibrium price falls but the quantity rises
Both the equilibrium price and quantity fall
Both the equilibrium price and quantity rise
The equilibrium price rises but the quantity falls

title: Market for wheat
questionText: A drought has reduced the wheat harvest, decreasing supply from S1 to S2, as shown. What has happened to the equilibrium price and quantity?

The equilibrium price falls but the quantity rises
Both the equilibrium price and quantity fall
The equilibrium price rises but the quantity falls

title: Market for electric cars
questionText: The diagram shows a shift in the market for electric cars, from D1 to D2. Which of the following could have caused it?
answers: A rise in the cost of the batteries used to make electric cars
A fall in the price of petrol cars, a substitute
A generous government rebate paid to consumers who buy an electric car
A new tax imposed on the sale of electric cars

title: Market for coffee
questionText: The diagram shows a large shift in the market for coffee, from S1 to S2. Which of the following could have caused it?
answers: A sharp rise in the wages of coffee farm workers
A fall in the wages of coffee farm workers
An increase in consumer incomes
The invention of a faster coffee-picking machine

title: Market for solar panels
questionText: The diagram shows a shift in the market for solar panels, from S1 to S2. Which of the following could have caused it?
answers: A rise in the price of the silicon used to make the panels
An increase in household demand for solar panels
A new tax imposed on solar panel manufacturers
A government subsidy paid to solar panel manufacturers

title: Market for sugary drinks
questionText: The diagram shows a shift in the market for sugary drinks, from D1 to D2. Which of the following could have caused it?
answers: A successful advertising campaign for sugary drinks

A fall in the price of sugar, an input

title: Market for cinema tickets
questionText: The diagram shows the market for cinema tickets in equilibrium. Household incomes then rise, and cinema tickets are a normal good. Which change will occur, and what will be its effect on the equilibrium?
answers: An increase in demand, raising both the equilibrium price and quantity
An increase in demand, lowering the price and raising the quantity
An increase in supply, lowering the price and raising the quantity
An increase in supply, raising both the equilibrium price and quantity

title: Market for televisions
questionText: The diagram shows the market for televisions in equilibrium. A new production technology then lowers manufacturers' costs. Which change will occur, and what will be its effect on the equilibrium?
answers: An increase in demand, raising both the equilibrium price and quantity
An increase in demand, lowering the price and raising the quantity
An increase in supply, lowering the price and raising the quantity
An increase in supply, raising both the equilibrium price and quantity

title: Market for red meat
questionText: The diagram shows the market for red meat in equilibrium. A health authority then warns that eating red meat raises the risk of disease. Which change will occur, and what will be its effect on the equilibrium?
answers: A decrease in supply, raising the price and lowering the quantity
A decrease in demand, lowering both the equilibrium price and quantity
A decrease in demand, raising the price and lowering the quantity
A decrease in supply, lowering both the equilibrium price and quantity

title: Market for bread
questionText: The diagram shows the market for bread in equilibrium. The price of flour, a key ingredient, then rises sharply. Which change will occur, and what will be its effect on the equilibrium?

A decrease in demand, raising the price and lowering the quantity
A decrease in supply, lowering both the equilibrium price and quantity
A decrease in supply, raising the price and lowering the quantity

title: Market for beef
questionText: In the beef market, demand and supply have both increased by the same amount, as shown. According to the diagram, what has happened to the equilibrium price and quantity?
answers: The equilibrium quantity rises, while the price stays the same
Both the equilibrium price and quantity rise
The equilibrium price rises, while the quantity stays the same
Both the equilibrium price and quantity fall

title: Market for face masks
questionText: The diagram shows the demand for face masks increasing from D1 to D2. The horizontal gap between D1 and D2 is the same at every price. Reading that gap from the diagram, by how much has demand increased at each price level?

By 40,000 masks

title: Market for rice
questionText: The rice market is in equilibrium at $5 per kg and 50 tonnes, as the diagram shows. Demand then increases, so that 20 more tonnes are demanded at every price. Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity.
answers: $6 per kg and 70 tonnes
$5 per kg and 70 tonnes
$6 per kg and 60 tonnes
$7 per kg and 60 tonnes

answers: $20 per kg and 120 tonnes
$20 per kg and 140 tonnes

questionText: When both demand and supply increase at the same time, which outcome is certain, even without knowing the size of each shift?
answers: The equilibrium price will rise
The equilibrium quantity will rise
The equilibrium price will stay the same
The equilibrium quantity will stay the same

title: Market for corn
questionText: The corn market is in equilibrium at $5 per kg and 50 tonnes, as shown. A trader wants the equilibrium price to rise to $7 per kg by increasing demand. By how much must demand increase at every price to achieve this? (Hint: read how much corn is supplied at $7, and how much is demanded at $7 on the current demand curve.)
answers: By 20 tonnes
By 70 tonnes
By 40 tonnes
By 30 tonnes

title: Market for timber
questionText: The timber market is in equilibrium at $25 per plank and 100,000 planks, as shown. The government wants the equilibrium price to fall to $15 per plank by increasing supply. By how much must supply increase at every price to achieve this? (Hint: read how much is demanded at $15, and how much is supplied at $15 on the current supply curve.)
answers: By 40,000 planks
By 140,000 planks
By 60,000 planks
By 80,000 planks
